audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal may bypass owner earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.328 billion present-value finance-lease liability and $2.192 billion contractual payments; liability equals 10.1% of $13.099 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Finance-lease ROU amortization may be added back in OE while principal remains in financing cash flow; total debt includes the liability but is context-only and therefore provides no valuation deduction
audit_findings.evidence: As of Dec. 31, 2025, other current liabilities and non-current finance lease liabilities include $ 37 million and $ 1.2 billion of finance lease obligations for these amended PPAs, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is demonstrated: latest total debt of $40.785 billion reconciles to $35.948 billion long-term debt, $999 million current maturities, $2.510 billion short-term debt and $1.328 billion finance leases. What remains unresolved is whether OE deducts the economic capital consumption or principal after adding back lease amortization. The liability's scale makes that possible omission material.
audit_findings.action: Trace the amended-PPA ROU additions, amortization, interest and principal through the 2025 OE workpaper; rerun all scenarios with any omitted principal or maintenance-equivalent capital charge, avoiding duplication of retained interest expense.

audit_findings.title: AFUDC can create noncash earnings and hide construction interest
audit_findings.magnitude: $281 million equity AFUDC plus $125 million debt AFUDC in 2025, or $406 million pre-tax—48.7% of the $834.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity AFUDC enters earnings without current cash, while debt AFUDC credits interest expense; both can inflate equity-level OE and its extrapolated growth base
audit_findings.evidence: The amount of AFUDC capitalized as a utility construction cost is credited to other nonoperating income (for equity capital) and interest charges (for debt capital).
audit_findings.explanation: The AFUDC amounts are demonstrated, but the record does not establish whether the OE calculation reversed them. Because the combined pre-tax amount approaches half the anchor, retention could materially raise every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Produce the 2025 OE reconciliation showing separate reversals of equity and debt AFUDC and their tax or regulatory offsets; rerun every scenario if either component remains in OE.

audit_findings.title: Unbounded wildfire claims may sit ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (filed context: $503 million of estimated losses and incurred legal costs, with approximately $80 million of insurance coverage remaining)
audit_findings.mechanism: Unreserved Smokehouse Creek claims, penalties or damages would reduce OE when paid or require a direct equity-bridge contingency deduction
audit_findings.evidence: This $ 430 million estimate does not include amounts for (i) potential penalties or fines that may be imposed by governmental entities on Xcel Energy, (ii) exemplary or punitive damages, (iii) compensation claims by federal, state, county and local government entities or agencies, (iv) unsettled compensation claims for damage to trees and oil and gas equipment, or (v) other amounts that are not reasonably estimable.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates a $460 million estimated loss, $43 million of incurred legal costs and limited remaining insurance, while expressly excluding several categories and stating that remaining claims could exceed coverage and materially affect the company. No incremental tail amount is estimable, so an additional valuation error is possible rather than demonstrated, but the filed risk is capable of being material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain claim, governmental-action, settlement and insurance-collectibility updates through 2026-09-05; estimate an insured and uninsured range and rerun the bridge or OE scenarios for the incremental equity exposure.

audit_findings.title: Future financing may break numerator-denominator coherence
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (filed context: $7.0 billion planned equity-credit funding through 2030; 69.7 million unsettled forward shares provide at least $5.2 billion)
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional common issuance increases the share denominator; equity-credit hybrids instead reduce future OE through financing costs, while the financed capital program supports the modeled growth numerator
audit_findings.evidence: Xcel Energy expects to fund additional capital investment with approximately 40% equity and 60% debt.
audit_findings.explanation: No present denominator error is demonstrated. The 695.546306 million share count is consistent with 624.634306 million latest outstanding shares, 69.7 million unsettled forwards and 1.212 million nonvested awards. The remaining financing mix is forward-looking, however, and further common issuance or hybrid costs could make the growth forecast and per-share denominator inconsistent.
audit_findings.action: At each financing or forward settlement, reconcile the complete $7.0 billion funding plan to issued shares, remaining forwards and hybrids; rerun per-share values using the resulting share count and include hybrid costs in OE.

audit_findings.title: Regulatory liabilities may represent unmodeled customer claims
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (latest filed regulatory liabilities total $7.440 billion versus the $2.010 billion cash/STI bridge addition)
audit_findings.mechanism: Customer refunds can reduce future revenue and OE, while obligations collected for future costs consume cash; omission could also make the gross cash bridge addition non-excess
audit_findings.evidence: Regulatory liabilities generally represent amounts that are expected to be refunded to customers in future rates or amounts collected in current rates for future costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The $7.440 billion liability balance is demonstrated and is 3.7 times the cash/STI addition, but it cannot be treated as a single equity claim. Major categories may be offset by deferred taxes, AROs, removal costs or other future expenses already reflected in OE. The record does not establish the net unmodeled shareholder effect or whether it is material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the latest current and noncurrent balances by category to refund schedules, associated costs, tax offsets and modeled OE; rerun the bridge only for cash that is restricted or economically committed and rerun OE for omitted revenue reductions.

audit_findings.title: Debt-extinguishment gains may inflate the 2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $162 million pre-tax in 2025, equal to 19.4% of the $834.2 million anchor; $56 million pre-tax in 2024
audit_findings.mechanism: A non-operating debt-repurchase gain enters net income and therefore OE unless explicitly purged, then propagates through forecast growth and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: On a consolidated basis, Xcel Energy Inc.’s repurchases of NSP-Minnesota first mortgage bonds were accounted for as debt extinguishments and resulted in pre-tax gains of approximately $ 162 million and $ 56 million in the years ended Dec. 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, net of unamortized discount and debt issuance costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains are demonstrated, but their inclusion in OE is not. The stated methodology identifies an interest-income purge without documenting removal of these gains. If the 2025 gain remains, its scale relative to the already depressed anchor is material; the valuation error is conditional on that unresolved inclusion.
audit_findings.action: Show the 2024 and 2025 OE workpaper lines for debt-extinguishment gains and related tax effects; if retained, remove them consistently from the historical series and rerun all scenarios without altering the selected growth rates or other inputs.
